To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the blockchain synchronization protocols can be optimized to minimize the traffic and energy consumption, depending on the security level and the synchronization frequency.

(1) a synchronization protocol that is based on the blockchain consensus protocol is the most secure and efficient, (2) the synchronization traffic scales with the number of accounts, (3) the synchronization traffic is inversely proportional to the number of validator nodes, and (4) the synchronization traffic increases with the number of IoT devices, while the power consumption of the synchronization protocol is inversely proportional.

(i) synchronization protocols with higher communication overheads have higher synchronization times, (ii) synchronization protocols with lower communication overheads have lower power consumption, and (iii) synchronization protocols with high communication overheads are less secure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of blockchain synchronization protocols for the IoT, and their analysis in terms of traffic generation, power consumption, and synchronization latency.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the communication traffic generated by the blockchain synchronization protocols is a key factor that affects the performance of the blockchain-powered IoT system, and the trade-offs between the communication traffic, the security level and the power consumption need to be carefully evaluated.
the communication cost of the synchronization protocols is a critical factor that affects the overall performance, in terms of both the power consumption of the IoT devices and the security level.
we provide an analytical model for the synchronization traffic of IoT devices, and we show that the synchronization traffic can be reduced by 50% with a negligible security loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the synchronization protocols have a significant impact on the communication cost of the IoT devices and that the choice of the protocol is strongly related to the security requirements and to the power consumption.
the communication overhead of the synchronization protocols is not negligible, and that it can be significantly reduced by exploiting the redundancy of the blockchain.

, in order to minimize the synchronization traffic, the IoT devices must be synchronized to the validator nodes via an intermediate node that is connected to the Internet and that has a larger bandwidth.
